name: Converse Modus Ponens (crossing lines)
description: R(x,y), ∀x∀y(R(x,y)→S(y,x)) ⊢ R(x,y)∧S(y,x) — modus ponens over a binary relation whose consequent swaps the arguments, so the two lines of identity cross. The tomos's first exemplar that exercises the Peirce bridge-at-crossing mark (Tier 3c, §3.0's worked example). Two steps (IT-, DC-) from the asserted premises; every step a real, attestable Dau-rule application.
